messages:
Sam: heads-up — seeing steady queue growth on ap-northeast p3 pool for model redwood-v2-med since ~14:05 UTC, backlog up ~3.2k tokens/sec over 20m. latency p50 climbed from 80ms -> 320ms.
Maya: link to dashboard?
Sam: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/queues?region=ap-northeast&pool=p3 — look at per-model queue depth and admission_control.rate_limit metrics.
Maya: ok seeing it. spikes coincide with spike in small chat completions from a single org id.
Leo: is this fairshare/pslot churn or actual compute shortage?
Sam: mix. pslot occupancy is near 100% for that model variant, preemption rate up. admission controller dropping only at p99.
Tess: cost question — if we spin up more p3s in ap-northeast on-demand that's expensive; cheaper to route to eu1/usw2?
Anita: eu1 has spare capacity but model variant there is quantized (redwood-v2-med-q4) — quality regression is ~0.7 BLEU in evals but for chat might be OK.
Leo: we should prefer routing policy over immediate scale if SLA permits. do a temporary routing rule: when queue_depth > 1500 for a model, route 30% traffic to eu1-q4. can be done via smart-routing.
Sam: agree. also want to reduce queue pressure locally: suggest lowering admission_control.max_inflight for that model from 350 -> 200 to shed excess quickly.
Maya: lowering max_inflight will increase client throttles — we should notify support/CS owners.
Tess: pinging @support on that org?
Maya: done — sent brief about transient throttling window and fallback to eu1.
ops-bot: alert: queue_growth_ap-northeast_p3 model=redwood-v2-med detected at 1802501600, severity=warning
Anita: another option is EVICITON policy tweak: currently LRU across pslots; we can pilot 'prefer-evict-large-batch' to free up small latency slots faster. Tradeoff: may impact throughput for batch jobs.
Leo: good call — run that as a short canary for 10m. If queue_depth drops 30% and p50 latency drops, keep. rollback otherwise.
Sam: running admission_control change now in ap-northeast for redwood-v2-med (max_inflight=200). also applying routing rule to send 30% -> eu1-q4 for that org id.
Maya: noticed immediate drop in new enqueued requests by ~18% in the console. p50 dropped to 210ms.
Tess: cost tracking note: estimate additional inter-region egress ~$45/hr if routing sustained. add to incident cost log.
Anita: starting pslot eviction policy canary in 2m with 10m window.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: config change applied (admission_control) by Sam at 1802501850 — rollout=instant, target=ap-northeast/redwood-v2-med
Leo: owners: Sam (triage), Anita (eviction canary), Maya (comms), Tess (cost). follow-up check in 20m.
Sam: will run a short eval on sample prompts against eu1-q4 to confirm no critical regressions.
Maya: support confirmed users see increased 429s for ~3min then fall back; they posted mitigation steps to the org.
Anita: eviction canary showing queue depth - 32% after 6m, p50 down to 180ms. no obvious throughput regressions.
Leo: sounds like plan: keep routing 30% -> eu1-q4 for next 30m, keep admission_control lowered, keep canary. if stable, we gradually shift to route 10% permanently and scale baseline next week if needed.
Tess: filing a quick follow-up doc for finance with cost delta and decision rationale.
Sam: updating incident ticket with actions and owners.
Maya: thanks team. will reconvene if metrics worsen. :thumbsup:
